questions.question_text: Which one of the following factors must the plaintiff prove to establish that malpractice has occurred?

options.text: A patient suffered a side effect from a medication that the doctor explained beforehand
Care of the patient was not optimal
Deviation from the standard of care caused damage to the patient
Safety planning failed to be done
That split treatment occurred

correct_answer.text: Deviation from the standard of care caused damage to the patient

correct_answers.text: Deviation from the standard of care caused damage to the patient

questions.explanation: To prove malpractice, The 4 Ds, must be proven—duty, deviation, damage, and direct causation (i.e., the deviation from the standard of care directly caused damage to the patient). If the doctor did not inform a patient of the risks of medication, there may be grounds for malpractice. Thus, it should always be documented that potential medication side effects have been reviewed. While one should strive for excellent care, only the standard of care needs to be met, and if not, malpractice can occur. Split treatment can be allowed, but the psychiatrist should be aware that they assume a collaborative or supervisory role with another mental health worker and that the patient's full responsibility lies in their care in split-treatment situations. (836)

questions.question_text: How frequently should a patient be seen for medication follow-up to avoid a malpractice claim?

options.text: As often as the psychiatrist feels is clinically indicated
At least once a year
At least once every 3 months
Every 2 weeks while medication is being titrated
Once a month if at least two medications are prescribed

correct_answer.text: As often as the psychiatrist feels is clinically indicated

correct_answers.text: As often as the psychiatrist feels is clinically indicated

questions.explanation: There are no standard rules or regulations set regarding how frequently patients should be monitored while on psychiatric medications. However, the longer time interval between visits can mean the higher likelihood of adverse drug reactions or new developments of clinical concerns. Though probably patients on medication should not go more than 6 months without being seen, psychiatrists should monitor patients for follow-up visits according to the patient's individual needs. (836)

questions.question_text: Which place or relationship is an exception to the law of privileged communications?

options.text: Doctor and patient
Husband and wife
Military courts
Priest and penitent
Social worker and patient

questions.explanation: Privilege, the right to maintain secrecy or confidentiality in the face of a subpoena, does not exist in the military courts, regardless of whether the physician is in the military. Privileged communications include husband–wife, priest–penitent, and doctor/therapist–patient relationships. (837)

questions.question_text: Courts scrutinize suicide cases and can hold the psychiatrist liable if the event was deemed to be:

options.text: Foreseeable
Impulsive
Predictable
Preventable
Secretive

questions.explanation: The law assumes that suicide is preventable if it is foreseeable. Courts scrutinize suicide cases to determine if the patient's suicide was foreseeable. It does not imply or require clinicians to be able to predict suicide or prevent it. (838)

questions.question_text: The first part of the Tarasoff law requires a psychiatrist to do which of the following when a patient reports intent to kill someone?

options.text: Document it and release the information to the courts
Hospitalize the patient involuntarily
Notify the victim and report the intended homicide
Report the patient's fantasies and dreams
Review a safety plan with the patient

correct_answer.text: Notify the victim and report the intended homicide

correct_answers.text: Notify the victim and report the intended homicide

questions.explanation: The 1976 case Tarasoff v. Regents of the University of California involved a patient reporting intent to kill a student. He was kept for 72 hours in an emergency room and the campus police were notified but upon release, he carried out the act and the girls' parents sued the university for negligence. The Tarasoff I ruling requires the therapist to report the intended homicide, and to notify the intended victim or others that they are in danger. This can include notifying the police to warn the intended victim. (839)

questions.question_text: The second part of the Tarasoff ruling (Tarasoff II) requires the psychiatrist to do which of the following actions?

options.text: Call the police
Maintain confidentiality
Notify family members
Prevent
Protect

questions.explanation: While the Tarasoff I ruling requires the psychiatrist to warn the intended victim, the Tarasoff II law has broadened the previous ruling requiring the duty to protect as well. The ruling prioritizes public safety over individual privacy. The duty to protect typically involves involuntary hospitalizations. Other steps such as calling the police and notifying family members can be involved with the first Tarasoff ruling. Though concerns that the patient won't be able to trust the doctor if confidentiality is maintained, if there is concern of imminent, serious harm, public safety trumps confidentiality. (839)

questions.question_text: Which is a key difference between a temporary versus an involuntary psychiatric admission?

options.text: A judge needs to release the patient
A writ of habeas corpus is necessary to be released
The patient cannot be held for typically more than 15 days
The next of kin must be notified in writing
Two physicians are required to sign the patient in

correct_answer.text: The patient cannot be held for typically more than 15 days

correct_answers.text: The patient cannot be held for typically more than 15 days

questions.explanation: Temporary admissions are utilized when a patient is confused and so impaired from a psychiatric standpoint that they need to be admitted on an emergency basis for their safety. One physician can recommend admission, whereas two physicians are required for an involuntary admission. After a temporary admission, the hospital staff must confirm the need for admission and that patients cannot be held against their will for a set period, typically 15 days. However, for an involuntary admission, the person can be held for a lengthy period as defined by the state, often around 60 days. The next of kin must be notified in writing of an involuntary hospitalization. The person can file for petition for a writ of habeas corpus to be released and the court must hear the case immediately. (840)

questions.question_text: Which of the following ethical principles should be considered when deciding to use seclusion or restraint for a patient?

options.text: Autonomy
Beneficence
Justice
Least restrictive alternative
Nonmaleficence

questions.explanation: The principle of least restrictive alternative holds that patients have the right to receive treatment using the least restrictive means (i.e., they should be treated as an outpatient, if possible, in an open ward, instead of seclusion, etc.). This principle should be considered when utilizing involuntary medication, seclusions, or restraints. (841)

questions.question_text: Which of the following measures should occur when utilizing seclusion or restraints?

options.text: A written order should be documented by a medical official
Documentation of evidence of an unstable psychiatric condition should be done
Proof of suicidal behavior should be noted
Release of the patient if consent is not obtained
The order needs to be reviewed every half hour

correct_answer.text: A written order should be documented by a medical official

correct_answers.text: A written order should be documented by a medical official

questions.explanation: For seclusion and restraints, a medical official must write an order and it should be time specified and the patient's condition must be regularly reviewed and documented. Extension must be reordered. These measures should only be implemented when the patient is at risk of harming themselves or others. Unless continuously monitored with constant direct observation, those patients with overtly suicidal behaviors should not be in seclusion or restraints. A contradiction to restraints include extremely unstable medical and psychiatric conditions. (841)

questions.question_text: Proving malpractice for a failure to obtain informed consent differs from other malpractice claims in which of the following ways?

options.text: Claims cannot be made if no other violation was performed
It can only include adverse medication side effects
Only minors can be involved
There is no requirement for an expert witness
There needs to be proof the patient was harmed

correct_answer.text: There is no requirement for an expert witness

correct_answers.text: There is no requirement for an expert witness

questions.explanation: Negligence to obtain informed consent is the one area of claim in which there is no requirement for expert testimony. While typically an expert witness is needed to prove departure from accepted medical practice, given the claim involves consent for treatment only, technically the outcome of the treatment does not need to be considered and there is no need to prove that the accepted standard of treatment was met. However, practically unless the treatment has adverse consequences, the complaint of failure to obtain consent typically does not get far. (842)

questions.question_text: A consent for treatment form should always include which of the following information?

options.text: A disclaimer that the patient is free to withdraw at any time
At least two patient identifiers
Conditions under which treatment must be adhered to
Information regarding only the gold standard of treatment
Signature by a witness

correct_answer.text: A disclaimer that the patient is free to withdraw at any time

correct_answers.text: A disclaimer that the patient is free to withdraw at any time

questions.explanation: Essential elements of a consent form include information about the procedure, purpose, identification of any experimental procedures, discomfort, and risks of the treatment as well as reasonable benefits to expect, alternatives to the procedure, and that the patient is free to withdraw consent and discontinue participation at any time. While more than one patient identifier on the form and a signature by a witness can be included, they are not essential features required for all consent forms. (842)

questions.question_text: What is necessary to declare a patient incompetent?

options.text: A judge's ruling in a court of law
Attestation by a forensic psychiatrist
Carrying a diagnosis of a severe mental illness
Having a prior guardian ad litem appointed
Possessing a physical handicap

correct_answer.text: A judge's ruling in a court of law

correct_answers.text: A judge's ruling in a court of law

questions.explanation: Competence is determined based on a person's ability to make a sound judgment, which include weighing in on the decision, reasoning, and making a reasonable decision. Competence is task specific. While physicians, typically psychiatrists, can give opinions of a person's competence, only a ruling by a judge can declare someone competent or incompetent. The diagnosis of a mental disorder alone is not sufficient to warrant incompetence, rather impairment must be noted. While a guardian is often appointed if someone is deemed incompetent, it is not mandatory to have one prior to declaring patient incompetent. (842)

questions.question_text: A patient with dementia acknowledges that she will lose ability to make decisions for herself soon. She creates a document while still of sound mind, indicating her sister can make decision for her when she is no longer able to act. This describes which of the following principles:

options.text: Contractual capacity
Durable power of attorney
Execution of competence
Guardian ad lidum
Testamentary competence

questions.explanation: A durable power of attorney is when a person appoints someone else to make decisions for them in anticipation of their loss of decision-making capacity. The patient documents a substitute decision maker that can act on their behalf without needing to involve a court proceeding. (843)

questions.question_text: According to the M'Naghten rule, to be found not guilty by reason of insanity, which of the following criteria must be met?

options.text: An expert witness must prove the defendant has a full, rather than a partial delusion
Only a diagnosis of bipolar, a delusional disorder, or schizophrenia can be applied
The accused does not know the difference between right and wrong in general
The act was caused by a delusion that led the accused to feel he was acting in self-defense
The accused must be proven by a psychiatrist to have a severe mental illness

correct_answer.text: The act was caused by a delusion that led the accused to feel he was acting in self-defense

correct_answers.text: The act was caused by a delusion that led the accused to feel he was acting in self-defense

questions.explanation: The M'Naghten rule gives guidelines for pleading insanity as a defense against criminal responsibility. To establish a defense of insanity, it must be clearly proven that at the time of committing the act, the patient acted under a defect of reason from an idea of the mind and did not know what he was doing was wrong. This can apply to a person if they have a partial delusion as well. The question is not whether the defendant knows the difference between right and wrong in general, but at the time of the act if the delusion caused them to not know right from wrong and feel they were acting in self-defense. (844)

questions.question_text: What is true of the verdict if someone is proven to be guilty, but mentally ill?

options.text: The accused must go to prison after psychiatric rehabilitation
The person is still labeled as a criminal but sent to an inpatient psychiatric unit
The person cannot be sentenced, as would be if proven not guilty by reason of insanity
The sentence is still imposed, and psychiatric treatment is delivered in prison
The sentence must be modified to the least restrictive criteria

correct_answer.text: The sentence is still imposed, and psychiatric treatment is delivered in prison

correct_answers.text: The sentence is still imposed, and psychiatric treatment is delivered in prison

questions.explanation: As an alternative to the verdict of guilty by reason of insanity, some states have established an alternative verdict of guilty, but mentally ill. However, the verdict if proven guilty but mentally ill is the same for other prisoners, in that if convinced, the accused will receive psychiatric treatment in prison, which is available to all prisoners as well. (844)

questions.question_text: Which of the following actions is most important, as advised by risk management, in recovered memory cases?

options.text: Avoid prescribing benzodiazepines
Begin a course of hypnosis to further help recover memories
Notify the police
Refer for a sodium amobarbital interview
Remain neutral and adhere to treatment boundaries

correct_answer.text: Remain neutral and adhere to treatment boundaries

correct_answers.text: Remain neutral and adhere to treatment boundaries

questions.explanation: There have been cases of therapist being sued for inducing false memories of sexual abuse. A fundamental allegation is that the therapist abandoned a position of neutrality to suggest or implant false childhood sexual memories. The guiding principle of clinical risk management in recovered memory cases is the maintenance of therapist neutrality and establishment of sound treatment boundaries. (844, 845)

questions.question_text: The Privacy Rule grants the patient which of the following privileges?

options.text: A release of information to insurance companies if separate forms are signed
Access to their records in only emergent situations
Ability to obtain copies of psychotherapy notes
Right to complain about violations to the police
Written notice of their rights

questions.explanation: The Privacy Rule, as administered by the Office for Civil Rights, mandates that physician must give the patient written notice of their privacy rights. Other mandates of this rule include that a patient can obtain copies of their medical records and that a physician can't limit a patient signing a release for records for nonroutine use. Patients have the right to complain if this rule is violated to the doctor, their health plan, or to the Secretary of HHS (the Federal Department of Health and Human Services). Patients are not permitted to obtain copies of their psychotherapy notes. Patients do not need to sign consent for release of information to health care plans for payment. (845)
